label: Update save name
summary: An action of the save game window that the game runs each time the player edits the save name.
details: Vanilla calls it from the name text box of the save game window whenever its text changes. It returns nothing; going by its name, it takes the typed text as the new save name.

label: Access saved ruler itself
summary: A function on a saved ruler of the ruler designer that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Age
summary: The age of a ruler saved in the ruler designer, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the window for loading a saved ruler design.

label: Culture
summary: The culture of a ruler saved in the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the culture section in the window for loading a saved ruler design, so the parts inside show that culture. The game documents no return type.

label: Daughters text
summary: A text about the daughters of a ruler saved in the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla puts it right after the married or single text and the sons text in the family line of the ruler design load window. Going by its name, it describes how many daughters the design has.

label: File name
summary: The file name of a saved ruler design.
details: Vanilla shows it as the entry's text in both the load and the save window of the ruler designer. The game documents no return type.

label: Skill list
summary: The list of skills of a ruler saved in the ruler designer, for the interface.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data model in the ruler design load window: one item per skill, each read with the SaveRulerSkillGui functions (icon frame, value, breakdown).

label: Trait list
summary: The list of traits of a ruler saved in the ruler designer, for the interface.
details: Vanilla shows it as a grid in the ruler design load window, each item read with SaveRulerTraitGui.GetTrait. It counts the list: up to 7 traits go in a plain grid, more in a scrolling box.

label: Rite
summary: The rite of a ruler saved in the ruler designer; vanilla reads a GetFaith function from it.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of the faith section in the ruler design load window and then reads Rite.GetFaith from it, so it is used to show the saved ruler's faith. It is also set as a data context inside the trait entries. The game documents no return type and nothing about what a rite is.

label: Sons text
summary: A text about the sons of a ruler saved in the ruler designer.
details: Vanilla puts it between the married or single text and the daughters text in the family line of the ruler design load window. Going by its name, it describes how many sons the design has.

label: Portrait image
summary: The portrait picture of a ruler saved in the ruler designer.
details: It takes three values that the game does not name. Going by vanilla's use, they are a portrait environment name, a camera name and the size of the widget. Vanilla passes `'environment_body', 'camera_body'` in the load window and `'environment_head', 'camera_head'` in the save window (the names suggest a full body picture versus a head picture), each with the widget's own screen size.

fields.name: environment
fields.text: Going by the values vanilla passes, the portrait environment.
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'environment_body' or 'environment_head'

fields.name: camera
fields.text: Going by the values vanilla passes, the portrait camera.
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'camera_body' or 'camera_head'

fields.name: size
fields.text: Going by the value vanilla passes, the size of the picture.

label: Used points
summary: How many ruler designer points a saved ruler design uses.
details: Vanilla shows the number in the load window and colours it by comparing it with the define NRulerDesigner IRONMAN_POINT_MAX: within the limit it is shown in the positive style, above it in the negative style.

label: Has sexuality
summary: Whether a ruler saved in the ruler designer has the given sexuality.
details: It takes the sexuality as a quoted name. The load window checks 'none', 'heterosexual', 'homosexual', 'bisexual' and 'asexual', and shows one element for each match.

fields.name: sexuality
fields.values: a quoted name such as 'heterosexual', 'homosexual' or 'none'

label: Is female
summary: Whether a ruler saved in the ruler designer is female.
details: Vanilla uses it in the load window to show different elements for female and non-female rulers, alone and together with the sexuality check.

label: Is married
summary: Whether a ruler saved in the ruler designer is married.
details: Vanilla uses it to write 'Married' or 'Single' at the start of the family line in the load window.

label: Select
summary: An action that selects this saved ruler design in the list.
details: Vanilla runs it when the player clicks an entry in the ruler designer save window. It returns nothing.

label: Saved ruler itself
summary: The saved ruler design entry itself, to hand to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the load and save windows' IsSelectedItem to show the selected entry as pressed. The game documents no return type.

label: Access skill entry itself
summary: A function on a skill entry of a saved ruler design that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Skill icon frame
summary: Which picture of the skill icon sheet to show for a skill of a saved ruler design.
details: Vanilla uses the number as the frame of gfx/interface/icons/icon_skills.dds in the ruler design load window, so each skill gets its own icon.

label: Skill breakdown
summary: The breakdown of what makes up a skill's value in a saved ruler design.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of the skill number in the load window and shows it as a tooltip when it has one (ValueBreakdown.HasTooltip). The game documents no return type.

label: Skill value
summary: The value of one skill of a saved ruler design.
details: Vanilla shows the number next to the skill icon in the ruler design load window.

label: Skill entry itself
summary: A function on a skill entry of a saved ruler design that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access trait entry itself
summary: A function on a trait entry of a saved ruler design that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait
summary: The trait shown by one trait entry of a saved ruler design.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of each trait icon in the ruler design load window. The game documents no return type.

label: Trait entry itself
summary: A function on a trait entry of a saved ruler design that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access scheme itself
summary: A function on a scheme that, going by its name, hands back the scheme itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Custom text
summary: A text made by a custom localization (a custom_loc entry), worked out for this scheme.
details: It takes the custom localization's key in quotes. Vanilla never uses it on a scheme; the same function on characters (Character.Custom('AIEconomicPersonality')) is a hint for how it is written.

label: Action name
summary: The scheme's action word, the part of its full name that comes before the target.
details: Vanilla builds a scheme's full action name from this followed by the target's name without tooltip (SCHEME_FULL_ACTION_NAME), and the same way for a predicted scheme in interactions.

label: Opportunities
summary: How many opportunities (charges the owner can spend on the scheme) the scheme has right now.
details: Vanilla shows the count in the scheme window, with one text for none ('No opportunities yet'), one for exactly one and one for more. The game HUD shows an element only when the player owns the scheme and this is above zero.

label: Breaches
summary: How many breaches the scheme has suffered so far.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'X out of Y', with Y from Scheme.GetSchemeType.GetMaximumBreaches.

label: Cooldown info
summary: A text about the scheme's cooldown, shown when the player is about to abandon the scheme.
details: Vanilla puts it at the end of the confirmation text "The ... against ... will be abandoned." What the text says exactly, the game does not show; going by the name, it tells what waiting time follows.

label: Paused reason
summary: The reason why the scheme is paused.
details: Vanilla shows it in the scheme window after 'Scheme is paused because'.

label: Full action name
summary: The full action name of the scheme, as used for a scheme entry's name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the name of a scheme entry in the scheme window and in the question about removing an agent from the scheme.

label: Maximum success chance
summary: The highest success chance the scheme can reach.
details: Vanilla shows the current chance 'out of' this number, and makes the current chance glow when the two are equal.

label: Scheme modifiers
summary: The list of modifiers that affect the scheme.
details: Vanilla shows it as a list in the intrigue window, each item read with the SchemeModifier functions, and shows something else when the list is empty. The game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: The name of the scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it in the scheme window's hint about spending opportunities on the scheme. Going by the names, GetNameNoTooltip is the same name without a tooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the scheme, without a tooltip attached.
details: Vanilla shows it as the title in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns (runs) the scheme.
details: Vanilla compares it with the player in the game HUD, which shows an element only for the player's own schemes that have opportunities. The game documents no return type.

label: Phases per opportunity
summary: How many scheme phases it takes to gain one opportunity.
details: Vanilla shows it as '1 opportunity gained per X phases' in the scheme window.

label: Phases until opportunity
summary: How many more scheme phases are left until the next opportunity.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'X phases until next opportunity' in the scheme window.

label: Progress
summary: How far the scheme has come towards its current goal, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla takes the goal (Scheme.GetProgressGoal) minus this value and shows the difference in days: the time until the next phase, or until completion for a basic scheme.

label: Progress bar value
summary: The scheme's progress as a decimal number for a progress bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a progress bar for the scheme in the game HUD.

label: Progress text
summary: A text describing the scheme's progress.
details: Vanilla uses it as the title of the scheme's progress tooltip, followed by the speed text and Scheme.GetResistanceDescription.

label: Progress goal
summary: The progress the scheme needs to reach its next phase, or completion.
details: Vanilla subtracts Scheme.GetProgress from it and shows the rest as days until the next phase or until completion.

label: Protecting countermeasure
summary: The scheme countermeasure that protects the scheme's target.
details: Vanilla builds a tooltip from it: the countermeasure's name, description, parameter list and owner modifiers. Countermeasures are measures a ruler can activate against schemes. The game documents no return type.

label: Scheme type
summary: The type of the scheme, which carries things like its maximum breaches and maximum secrecy.
details: Vanilla reads the type's limits from it, such as the maximum number of breaches and the maximum secrecy.

label: Secrecy
summary: The scheme's secrecy, shown as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it in the scheme window and its preparations window, and in the secrecy tooltip next to the type's maximum (Scheme.GetSchemeType.MaxSecrecy).

label: Secrecy text
summary: A text explaining the scheme's secrecy.
details: Vanilla shows it in the secrecy tooltip below the current and maximum secrecy.

label: Speed
summary: A whole number on a scheme that takes one value; going by its name, the scheme's speed.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the game does not say what the value it takes is.

label: Speed text
summary: A text explaining the scheme's speed.
details: Vanilla shows it in the scheme window's progress breakdown and in the progress tooltip.

label: Success chance
summary: The scheme's current chance of success.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage 'out of' Scheme.GetMaxSuccessChance, glowing when it has reached that maximum.

label: Success chance text
summary: A text explaining the scheme's success chance.
details: Vanilla shows it in the success chance tooltip of the scheme window.

label: Success chance growth
summary: How much the scheme's success chance grows per phase.
details: Vanilla shows it as a signed percentage per phase in brackets after the current success chance.

label: Target
summary: The scheme's target, as a general scheme target.
details: The target can be a character or something else (the scheme also has GetTargetCharacter, GetTargetTitle and others). Vanilla reads its name in scheme tooltips ("Target: ..."), in effect texts about leaving a scheme, and without tooltip in the scheme's full action name.

label: Target character
summary: The character the scheme is aimed at.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the game HUD and in the intrigue window.

label: Target culture
summary: The culture the scheme is aimed at.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the game HUD and in the intrigue window.

label: Target faith
summary: The faith the scheme is aimed at.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the game HUD and in the intrigue window.

label: Target title
summary: The title the scheme is aimed at.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the game HUD and in the intrigue window, and a scheme text uses the title's possessive name for a scheme that takes gold from the title's treasury.

label: Task contract
summary: The task contract linked to the scheme.
details: Vanilla shows its name only in debug mode, as 'Contract: ...' in the intrigue window. The game documents no return type.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the scheme.
details: Vanilla shows it under 'Scheme:' in the bottom bar's scheme tooltip and under 'Puppet Scheme:' in the puppet view.

label: Type description
summary: A text describing the scheme's type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the scheme window's tooltip and in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Has task contract
summary: Whether the scheme is linked to a task contract.
details: Vanilla uses it together with debug mode to show the contract's name in the intrigue window.

label: Is exposed
summary: Whether the scheme has been exposed.
details: Vanilla shows an element in the game HUD and in the intrigue window when this is true.

label: Is paused
summary: Whether the scheme is paused and makes no progress.
details: Vanilla shows a paused element in the intrigue window when this is true; Scheme.GetFrozenReason gives the reason.

label: Is secret
summary: Whether the scheme is secret.
details: Vanilla shows secrecy elements in the intrigue window when this is true.

label: Is not paused
summary: Whether the scheme is running, not paused.
details: Vanilla shows the time until the next phase (or completion) in the intrigue window only when this is true.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether this is a real scheme, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never names it on Scheme; IsValid on other types (such as a government) checks that something exists, which is a hint at most.

label: Script scope
summary: The scheme as a script scope, so the interface can read its variables and script values.
details: Vanilla uses it to read the scheme variable 'secrecy_grace_period' (months of secrecy grace left) and script values such as 'scheme_charge_to_advance_threshold_value'.

label: Scheme itself
summary: The scheme itself, to hand to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the intrigue window's cancel action when the player clicks to cancel a scheme. The game documents no return type.

label: Access agent slot itself
summary: A function on an agent slot of a scheme that, going by its name, hands back the slot entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Agent
summary: The agent character who fills this slot of a scheme.
details: Vanilla shows the agent's name in the agent tooltip and sets the character as the data context of the slot in the intrigue window. The game documents no return type.

label: Contribution
summary: How much the agent in this slot adds to the scheme's speed.
details: The agent tooltip lists it as a signed number under scheme speed. The intrigue window shows it rounded to a whole number on the slot.

label: Contribution breakdown
summary: A text breaking down what makes up the slot's contribution to the scheme.
details: Vanilla shows it under the contribution text in the slot's contribution tooltip.

label: Contribution text
summary: A text describing what this agent slot contributes to the scheme.
details: Vanilla shows it in the contribution tooltip both for a filled slot (with the breakdown) and for an empty one (alone).

label: Contribution icon
summary: The icon for what this agent slot contributes to the scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it as a picture on the slot in the intrigue window. The game documents no return type.

label: Slot
summary: The agent slot itself, with its slot type.
details: Vanilla reads the slot's name, and through GetSlotType its type's name and description, to label the slot and its tooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Is exposed
summary: Whether the agent in this slot has been exposed.
details: Vanilla shows an exposed marker on the slot in the intrigue window when this is true.

label: Is filled
summary: Whether an agent fills this slot of the scheme.
details: Vanilla picks the slot's tooltip by it (a full one for a filled slot, a shorter one for an empty slot) and shows parts of the slot only when it is filled.

label: Remove agent
summary: A command that removes the agent from this slot of the scheme.
details: Vanilla opens it as a confirmation popup when the player clicks the remove button on a slot; the question reads 'Remove ... as agent from the ... scheme?'.

label: Agent slot itself
summary: The agent slot entry itself, to hand to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to SchemeItem.ShowPotentialAgents when the player clicks a slot, to list the characters who could fill it. The game documents no return type.

label: Access countermeasure itself
summary: A function on a scheme countermeasure type that, going by its name, hands back the countermeasure itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Activation cost text
summary: A text listing what it costs the given character to activate this scheme countermeasure.
details: It takes the character who would pay. Vanilla passes Character.Self and shows the text under 'Activation cost:'.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character who would activate it.

label: Description
summary: The description of the scheme countermeasure.
details: Vanilla shows it at the end of the countermeasure activation text, after the parameters, cost and modifiers.

label: Frame
summary: A picture used as the frame of the scheme countermeasure.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the intrigue window. The game documents no return type.

label: Frame path
summary: A text on a scheme countermeasure type; going by its name, the file path of its frame picture.
details: Vanilla never uses it. SchemeCountermeasureType.GetFrame gives the frame picture itself.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of the scheme countermeasure.
details: Vanilla shows it in the game HUD and in the intrigue window. The game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: The name of the scheme countermeasure.
details: Vanilla uses it as the title of the countermeasure's tooltip and in 'Activate ...' and 'Deactivate ...'.

label: Owner modifiers text
summary: A text listing the countermeasure's owner modifiers.
details: Going by its name, these are modifiers the owner of the countermeasure gets. Vanilla shows it under 'Modifiers:' in the activation text and in the tooltip of a countermeasure protecting a scheme's target.

label: Parameter list text
summary: A text listing the countermeasure's parameters.
details: Vanilla shows it at the start of the activation text when the countermeasure has parameters, and in the tooltip of a countermeasure protecting a scheme's target.

label: Has activation cost
summary: Whether activating the scheme countermeasure costs something.
details: Vanilla shows the activation cost section only when this is true.

label: Has icon
summary: A function on a scheme countermeasure type that, going by its name, tells whether it has an icon.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; HasIcon on other types (laws, game concepts) decides whether an icon is shown, which is a hint at most. The game documents no return type.

label: Has owner modifiers
summary: Whether the countermeasure has owner modifiers to list.
details: Vanilla shows the modifiers section of the activation text only when this is true.

label: Has parameters
summary: Whether the countermeasure has parameters to list.
details: Vanilla shows the parameter list of the activation text only when this is true.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether there is a real scheme countermeasure here.
details: Vanilla shows the countermeasure's elements in the game HUD and the intrigue window only when this is true, so going by that use it checks that a countermeasure is set.

label: Countermeasure itself
summary: A function on a scheme countermeasure type that, going by its name, hands back the countermeasure itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access scheme entry itself
summary: A function on a scheme entry of the intrigue window that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Are members shown
summary: Whether the member list of a scheme entry is shown, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it on scheme entries; the faction window uses FactionItem.AreMembersVisible to show a faction's member list, which is a hint at most.

label: Can cancel
summary: Whether the player can cancel this scheme.
details: Vanilla enables the cancel button of the scheme entry only when this is true; SchemeItem.GetCancelSchemeDescription gives its tooltip.

label: Agent slots
summary: The list of agent slots of the scheme entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as a list in the intrigue window, each item read with the SchemeAgentSlotItem functions. The game documents no return type.

label: Cancel text
summary: The tooltip text of the scheme entry's cancel button.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the cancel button in the intrigue window.

label: Agent slot count
summary: The total number of agent slots of the scheme entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as the total in 'X out of Y agent slots filled', with the scheme's script value 'current_scheme_filled_agent_slots_value' as X.

label: Progress level tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for one step of the scheme's progress bar.
details: It takes the step's position. Vanilla passes the widget's index in its list (PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel), in the intrigue and situation windows.

fields.name: index
fields.text: Which step of the progress bar.
fields.values: a whole number; vanilla gives PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel

label: Progress levels
summary: The steps of the scheme's success progress bar.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of the success progress bar in the intrigue window. The game documents no return type.

label: Scheme
summary: The scheme shown by this entry of the intrigue window.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context and reads the scheme's name and script values from it through MakeScope. The game documents no return type.

label: Show or hide members text
summary: A text on a scheme entry; going by its name, the tooltip of a button that shows or hides the member list.
details: Vanilla never uses it on scheme entries; the faction window uses FactionItem.GetShowHideMembersTooltip that way, which is a hint at most.

label: Show members frame
summary: A whole number on a scheme entry; going by its name, which picture to show on the show-members button.
details: Vanilla never uses it on scheme entries; the faction window uses FactionItem.GetShowMembersFrame as a frame number, which is a hint at most.

label: Has agents
summary: Whether the scheme entry has any agents.
details: Vanilla enables a button only when this is true and shows something else when it is false.

label: Cancel
summary: An action the game runs when the player clicks the scheme entry's cancel button.
details: The button is enabled only when SchemeItem.CanCancelScheme is true. It returns nothing.

label: Scheme entry itself
summary: A function on a scheme entry of the intrigue window that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Show or hide members
summary: An action on a scheme entry; going by its name, it shows or hides the member list.
details: Vanilla never uses it on scheme entries; the faction window runs FactionItem.ShowHideMembersFrame on a click, which is a hint at most. It returns nothing.

label: Show potential agents
summary: An action that, going by its name, shows the characters who could fill the given agent slot.
details: It takes the slot. Vanilla runs it when the player clicks an empty-slot portrait in the intrigue window, passing SchemeAgentSlotItem.Self. It returns nothing.

fields.name: slot
fields.text: The agent slot to find agents for.
fields.values: an agent slot, for example SchemeAgentSlotItem.Self

label: Open scheme
summary: A command the game sends when the player clicks a scheme entry with preparations.
details: Vanilla posts it on left and right click of the entry for schemes that are not basic; the entry's tooltip says to spend opportunities to interact with the scheme. Going by its name, it does what clicking the scheme in the top bar does.

label: Access scheme modifier itself
summary: A function on a scheme modifier that, going by its name, hands back the modifier itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Description
summary: The text of one modifier that affects a scheme.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of each entry in the scheme's modifier list in the intrigue window.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of one modifier that affects a scheme.
details: Vanilla shows it on each entry of the scheme's modifier list. The game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: A text on a scheme modifier; going by its name, the modifier's name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetName on other types gives their names, which is a hint at most.

label: Static modifier
summary: The static modifier behind this scheme modifier, going by its name.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the scheme's modifier list. The game documents no return type and nothing about what a static modifier is.

label: Scheme modifier itself
summary: A function on a scheme modifier that, going by its name, hands back the modifier itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access pulse action itself
summary: A function on a scheme pulse action that, going by its name, hands back the action itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type and nothing about what a scheme pulse action is.

label: Pulse action itself
summary: A function on a scheme pulse action that, going by its name, hands back the action itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access target itself
summary: A function on a scheme target that, going by its name, hands back the target itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Name
summary: The name of a scheme's target.
details: Vanilla reads it through Scheme.GetTarget, for example "Target: [SCHEME.GetTarget.GetName]" in the scheme tooltip and in the text about someone no longer being part of a scheme against the target.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of a scheme's target as plain text, without the tooltip names usually carry.
details: Vanilla uses it for the scheme's full action name: the action word (GetActionName) followed by this name.

label: Target itself
summary: A function on a scheme target that, going by its name, hands back the target itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access scheme type itself
summary: A function on a scheme type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Action name
summary: A text on a scheme type; going by its name, the type's action name.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Its texts write GetActionName after a scheme (SCHEME.GetActionName), which is only a hint.

label: Category name
summary: The name of the scheme type's category.
details: Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout, formatted as a game concept link.

label: Detailed description
summary: The long description of the scheme type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout.

label: General description
summary: A text on a scheme type; going by its name, the type's general description.
details: Vanilla never uses it. SchemeType.GetDetailedDescription is the description vanilla shows.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of the scheme type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout. The game documents no return type.

label: Illustration
summary: The illustration of the scheme type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a picture in the interaction window templates. The game documents no return type.

label: Maximum breaches
summary: How many breaches a scheme of this type can have at most.
details: Breaches are a scheme game concept (scheme_breaches_short). Vanilla's scheme window shows a scheme's breaches as "X out of Y" and "X/Y", with this number as Y, read through Scheme.GetSchemeType.

label: Type name
summary: The name of the scheme type.
details: In the lines given, vanilla shows it in a debug window that watches the AI.

label: Type name without tooltip
summary: The name of the scheme type, without a tooltip attached.
details: Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Has icon
summary: A function on a scheme type that, going by its name, tells whether it has an icon.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; HasIcon on other types (laws, game concepts) decides whether an icon is shown, which is a hint at most. The game documents no return type.

label: Is basic
summary: Whether the scheme type is a basic scheme.
details: Vanilla's intrigue window reads it through Scheme.GetSchemeType: for a basic scheme it shows the basic progress text (SCHEME_WINDOW_PROGRESS_INFO_BASIC) instead of the normal one, and shows or hides parts of the scheme entry by it.

label: Is contract
summary: Whether the scheme type is a contract scheme, going by its name.
details: Vanilla reads it as scheme.GetSchemeType.IsContract in the invite-agent interaction, to word the invite as an order to a follower; that line is a hint, not named on this type directly.

label: Is hostile
summary: Whether the scheme type is a hostile scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it in the interaction window templates to show or hide parts depending on whether the scheme type is hostile.

label: Is personal
summary: Whether the scheme type is a personal scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it in the interaction window templates to show or hide parts depending on whether the scheme type is personal.

label: Is political
summary: Whether the scheme type is a political scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it in the interaction window templates to show or hide parts depending on whether the scheme type is political.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether there really is a scheme type here.
details: Vanilla uses it to show scheme parts only when there is one: in interaction items (InteractionItem.GetSchemeType.IsValid) and in the event window's scheme widgets (Scheme.GetSchemeType.IsValid).

label: Maximum secrecy
summary: The highest secrecy a scheme of this type can have, as a percentage.
details: Vanilla shows it as "(max X%)" after the scheme's current secrecy in the secrecy tooltips, read through Scheme.GetSchemeType.

label: Maximum success
summary: A whole number on a scheme type; going by its name, the highest success chance its schemes can reach.
details: Vanilla never uses it. Scheme.GetMaxSuccessChance is what vanilla shows for a running scheme.

label: Scheme type itself
summary: A function on a scheme type that, going by its name, hands back the type itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access scope itself
summary: A function on a script scope that, going by its name, hands back the scope itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: As accolade
summary: A function of the script system on a script scope; going by its name, it reads the scope as an accolade (an honour a liege gives a knight).
details: Vanilla never uses it; the lines given only mention accolades as a game concept. The game documents nothing more than 'Jomini Script System' and no return type.

label: As activity
summary: The script object read as an activity (a special occasion such as a hunt or feast).
details: Vanilla texts use it on the main object, ROOT.Activity, then read the activity's name or its current phase and that phase's location, as in the hunt texts about the terrain. The game documents no return type.

label: As activity type
summary: A function of the script system on a script scope; going by its name, it reads the scope as an activity type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; the line given uses ActivityType as a type of its own, which is a hint at most. The game documents nothing more than 'Jomini Script System' and no return type.

label: As army
summary: The script object read as an army.
details: Vanilla's one use is the short label text for an army (SCOPE_ARMY), ROOT.Army.GetName followed by a colon; the game defines such a label for each kind of object. The game documents no return type.

label: As artifact
summary: A function of the script system on a script scope; going by its name and its use as a data context, it reads the scope as an artifact.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in the situation list and in the artifact rewards of the activity window, so the parts inside show that artifact. The game documents nothing more than 'Jomini Script System' and no return type.
